Lotus Root 12.5.1 · 20 Nov 2026

Ready for the Napoleon fork

⬇ Download 12.5.1What is newQuick start
ImportantNapoleon, 2026-12-21 20:50 UTC: every node must run 12.5.1 or later before then. This version qualifies. Until Napoleon it follows the same rules as 12.4.x, so you can upgrade now. Earlier versions, 12.4.x included, do not follow the chain after the fork.

Highlights

  • Merged mining on real parent chains. From Napoleon, merged-mined blocks must be anchored to real Bitcoin, eCash, Bitcoin Cash or Litecoin blocks.
  • Pools: one setting for SHA-256d. Litecoin pools that already merge-mine Lotus with standard AuxPoW need no change. SHA-256d pools (eCash, Bitcoin, Bitcoin Cash) name their chain in one place: createauxblock <address> xec|btc|bch, or -auxpowalgo=<chain> on the Lotus node.
  • One difficulty lane per parent chain. From Napoleon, merged mining on Bitcoin, eCash, Bitcoin Cash and Litecoin each has its own difficulty, and a miner picks the chain by its stratum port. Merged mining cannot crowd out native mining.
  • Parent chains in the dashboard. The explorer and the network pages show the parent chains Lotus follows.
  • Rewards spendable sooner. From Napoleon, block rewards and pool payouts can be spent after 20 blocks (about 40 minutes).
  • Upgrade notice. The node tells you when a newer version is announced by enough of its peers.

Compatibility and rollback

Minimum version on the network12.5.1, required from Napoleon (2026-12-21 20:50 UTC)
NapoleonEvery node must run 12.5.1 or later before 2026-12-21 20:50 UTC. This version qualifies.
UpgradingStop the node, replace the binaries, start it. The data directory is kept.
Going backStop the node and put the previous binaries back. Going back is not always possible once a newer version has written to the data directory; the release says when.

Install and verify

Docker 
docker pull ghcr.io/lotusdevorg/lotusd:12.5.1
docker run -d --name lotusd -v lotus-data:/data ghcr.io/lotusdevorg/lotusd:12.5.1
Linux 
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/LotusDevOrg/lotusd-releases/releases/download/v12.5.1/SHA256SUMS
curl -fsSLO https://github.com/LotusDevOrg/lotusd-releases/releases/download/v12.5.1/lotus-binaries-12.5.1-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS     # must print: OK
tar -xzf lotus-binaries-12.5.1-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
./lotus-binaries-12.5.1-linux-x86_64/lotusd -version
macOS

The same steps with lotus-binaries-12.5.1-macos-x86_64.tar.gz; check with shasum -a 256 -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS. macOS asks for confirmation before the first launch (the binaries are not notarised).

Windows

Download lotus-binaries-12.5.1-windows-x86_64.zip and SHA256SUMS. In PowerShell, Get-FileHash .\lotus-binaries-12.5.1-windows-x86_64.zip -Algorithm SHA256 must give the value on that file's line. Then unzip.

Download Lotus binaries from github.com/LotusDevOrg/lotusd-releases only, and check them against SHA256SUMS.
